title: Product-Market Fit Engine
content:
Original paraphrased demo notes based on Rahul Vohra's Lenny's Podcast discussion. These are not verbatim transcript excerpts.

Rahul Vohra describes a practical way to turn product-market fit into a measurable product loop. The starting point is the Sean Ellis style survey question asking users how disappointed they would be if they could no longer use the product.

The important segment is the group that says they would be somewhat disappointed. Vohra's approach is to understand why the strongest users love the product, then look for somewhat-disappointed users who share that same core reason for valuing it. Those users become the most useful audience for improving the product-market fit score.

The framework deliberately avoids treating every piece of feedback equally. Users who are not disappointed may not yet have experienced enough value, while users who are very disappointed already provide evidence of the product's strongest value. The middle group can reveal objections that are close enough to the core value proposition to be actionable.

Superhuman used this approach to keep product decisions concentrated around a specific value proposition rather than adding unrelated requests to the roadmap. The lesson is not simply to chase a benchmark; it is to create a repeatable measurement-and-improvement loop.

Vohra also discusses manual onboarding as an early-stage tactic. Hands-on onboarding can create strong user relationships, reveal friction directly, and delay expensive self-service automation until the team understands what great activation looks like.

Key themes: PMF measurement, very-disappointed users, somewhat-disappointed users, focused feedback, value proposition alignment, manual onboarding, and iterative product improvement.
